_step150: the shot leaves on a tap's release (planning step 137): each tap goes down on `tick` and comes up on `release`, the next tick unless it says later
_about: 4-02 (level1c), the designers' own solution, GOLD (golden_score 1, 3 crystals): ONE shot, aimed AWAY from where the player wants to go. The level is weightless (`no_gravity`): there is no walking, and every accepted tap shoves the player 140 u/s (zerog.json, 1.4 m/s) directly away from the shot's end, with no drag (F10: 'additive, with no drag').

The player stands on the block at (138, 152), the three crystals hang at y 154 (x 212, 244, 274: 2 units off his own height) and the door is at x 344: a shot to the LEFT at his own height sends him straight right through all three crystals into the door. Here the tap is at (40, 152) on tick 40: the shot lands a portal in empty space at the tap's point (the one portal the golden score counts, opened on tick 65, after he has taken the first crystal) and he glides right at 140 u/s with a vertical speed of 0, takes the crystals on ticks 63, 77 and 90 and touches the door on tick 124. Nothing else is pressed.

WHY THE RECORDED ROUTE (tests/routes/level1c.json, won on tick 87, medal 1, 2 portals, 0 crystals) WAS NOT THIS: it shot AT the door (the recoil pushes him LEFT, away from the crystals and the door, to the view's edge) and spent a second portal on himself to be carried through the portal in the door. It wins and misses gold on both counts. This route has no portal pair: the portal it places is never entered.

Margins (each input moved alone, all others kept; ticks, or level units for a point): 12 of 12 variants win and earn medal 3 (the tap's tick -8, -2, +2, +8; its x -6, -2, +2, +6; its y -6, -2, +2, +6). The tick has no upper edge (any tick from 26 to 400 that was tried is gold: he waits on the block and nothing moves him); a tap on tick 24 or earlier is refused ('the 400 ms between taps'; tick 25 is the first accepted). The aim band at tick 40, x 40: every y from 2 to 173 is gold; y 176 and 179 win with medal 2 (the glide rises 13.7 degrees and misses the third crystal), y 182 and below do not win. These are the PORT's numbers (body-overlap pick, friction 0); the original's band is not known and is likely tighter (see below). Only the near-horizontal aim at his own height is independent of both.

NOT MEASURED ON THE ORIGINAL: (1) the recoil's speed at 60 Hz: F10 measured a shot at 40 to 44 u/s on an emulator running 17 to 19 frames a second, and the decode (a fixed 1/30 s Box2D step) says 70 u/s of physics time = 140 u/s at a 60 Hz frame; nothing here depends on the speed but the time to the door. (2) A body gliding along the TOP of a static block under zero gravity: the port's player has friction 0 (Player kFriction), the original's dark_mage.ent 0.9 (backlog R4a-2). With an exactly horizontal aim nothing presses him into the block, so friction cannot act; a tap ABOVE his height presses him down, and there the original would lose speed to the block (about vx = 140 (cos a - 0.9 sin a), model not measurement) where the port loses none: the route keeps to a horizontal aim. (3) The crystal pick: the port takes a crystal when the player's body overlaps its 28 x 24 box; the original's `MainCharacter::crystalPicker` takes it when his POINT is within squaredRange of the crystal's point (backlog Order 10.2, open; the range is not decoded here). This glide passes each crystal's point at 2 units, so any range above about 3 units takes all three. (4) That the original opens a portal in empty space at the tap point and counts it as one (decoded: computePortalFinalPos with no hit is the aim itself); a failed shot would count 0 and still be gold.
